Lydia — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and the current Redwood defaults (also reflected in the attached matrix):

- Retention defaults (configurable per-customer):
  * Token-level ephemeral logs (trace-level request bodies): 30 days (default) — retained for debugging, then purged/crypto-delete.
  * Structured request and routing logs (metadata, model/route, latency): 180 days (default).
  * Backups & snapshots (binary snapshots and cold archives): 365 days (default archival TTL).

- Snapshots & deletion SLA: snapshots are considered separate custodial copies. Standard account deletion request triggers deletion of live data and routine logs; archived snapshots are removed through a controlled erase workflow: we perform a targetted purge from active stores and then rotate the snapshot keys or crypto-delete archived blobs. Because snapshots can be copied to WORM-style object storage for long-term retention, we require a formal erase request to remove archived copies and a short verification window (we typically commit to a 30-90 day window for completing archived cleanup depending on region and storage provider constraints). This is an "exception" to instantaneous deletion and is surfaced in the DPA as a backup/snapshot erase appendix.

- Audit-style deletion evidence: we can provide a time-stamped audit record that includes: request id, account id, scope (keys/objects removed), deletion method (crypto-delete, overwrite, key-rotation), operator id, and completion timestamp. I’ve attached a sample snippet format in the retention matrix (see the "deletion-audit-sample" tab in log-ttl-draft.xlsx).

- SOC 2 status: Redwood has completed Type I for the current control set and we expect Type II covering the current production controls to be available by Q3 2027 (target August 2027). We can share the report under NDA or provide an interim bridge letter for your risk team — let us know which you prefer.

- Legal holds: if Atlas requires legal hold, we map that to an exception and do not perform snapshot deletion until notice is lifted; we document legal hold start/stop in the audit trail.

Next steps for us to formalize:
1) Rohan: confirm whether Atlas needs the archive erase window shortened (e.g., to 30 days) or if the 30–90 day window is acceptable.
2) Lydia: once you return the questionnaire, Ben will review and mark any control gaps / contract appendix asks.
3) If contract appendices are needed, we’ll surface the exact language for the DPA and a backup-erase SLA.

Happy to jump on a call to walk your security ops through the matrix.

—Ben
